phase: Issue #154 Phase 2-C2.5-D2-b: Chrome Dedicated Worker re-measurement after the D2-a Ideal-only publication (post-hoc analysis)

environment.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/153.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

heapLimits.note: The page realm limit is another realm's value, given for reference only. The Dedicated Worker used heap is the external CDP sample (runs[].cdp). The Dedicated Worker's own limit is unknown unless the Worker realm reported one. Neither is compared with Node.

conditions.workerPolicy: one fresh Dedicated Worker per run
conditions.repeatPolicy: Phase 2-C2.5-B rule, unchanged: a context whose attempt 1 pair had a page / browser crash, a native Worker failure, a mode disagreement or a CDP attach failure is run once more (at most 2 attempts); both attempts are kept
conditions.classificationPolicy: Phase 2-C2.5-B pre-registered rule, unchanged (phase2c25bPairClassification); an explicit V8 OOM crash key is auxiliary only
conditions.formalSeriesPolicy: validatePhase2C25D2BFormalSeries(): every workload context has exactly one attempt 1 minimal / instrumented run; the repeat decision recomputed by phase2c25bRepeatDecision() equals the recorded one; exactly one attempt 2 pair where it repeats and none otherwise; no attempt above 2, foreign context, duplicate run or extra / missing decision; driver modes exactly minimal + instrumented, allowRepeat true, only null, completedAt present. Checked before the analysis; a failure ends the analyzer without a result.

formal: Context parity: before any Search, every page session re-derived the workload orientations from the original Export and matched the Phase 2-C2.5-A evidence field by field (digests included).
Controls: 2 / 2 ended normally in both modes with equal Browser semantics, equal to Node D2-a in status, Search summary, first Candidate key, extent / exhaustion and instrumented prediction counts.

Formal Browser classification per context (Phase 2-C2.5-B rule, unchanged): c0-p0#0 browser_no_failure (before: inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash); c12-p0#0 inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash (before: inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash); c2-p1#0 inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash (before: inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash); c8-p1#0 browser_no_failure (before: browser_no_failure); c13-p4#0 browser_no_failure (before: browser_no_failure). Overall: mixed.

After the D2-a Ideal-only publication, c0-p0#0 no longer reproduced the Phase 2-C2.5-B renderer loss in the Chrome Dedicated Worker: both modes ended stopped_by_extent_before_candidate, equal to Node D2-a in status, Search summary, first Candidate key, extent / exhaustion and instrumented prediction counts.

Auxiliary: 8 / 10 representative runs carry an explicit V8 OOM crash key in their renderer crash dump (explicit_v8_oom_crash_key, beside the formal classification); 8 lost the renderer while the Search Worker ran, before any first Candidate notice.
Run outcomes: 14 runs; first Candidate reached 2; renderer (page) loss 8; browser loss 0; native Worker failure 0; structured error 0; timeout 0.
notYet: That the Browser memory problem is solved: c12-p0#0 (inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash), c2-p1#0 (inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash) still did not end normally in the Chrome Dedicated Worker.

A memory-efficiency multiple from the CDP samples: they are sampled (about 500 ms), include uncollected garbage, and a lost run is cut at the loss; progress ratios below describe how far the Search got, not bytes per state.

The Dedicated Worker's own heap limit. Heap measurement boundary: the Dedicated Worker used heap sampled by CDP reached 1.95-3.38 GiB (per-run sampled maxima) in the representative runs (normal terminations and losses alike); the page realm reported performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit 4395630592 bytes (about 4.09 GiB), a value of another realm given for reference only; the Dedicated Worker realm did not expose its own jsHeapSizeLimit, so the Worker's actual heap limit was not measured (unknown) and is not taken to equal the page realm value. Neither value is compared directly with the Node 8 GB heap limit.
A heap comparison with Node D2-a: Node heap bytes and limits are not compared with the Browser (different runtimes; the sampled Browser maximum over all runs was 3.38 GiB).
